# UMass Global Announces Revamped 30-Credit Masters of Business Administration Programs

Published: September 1st, 2026

Image

ALISO VIEJO, Calif. (September 1, 2026) — University of Massachusetts Global announces the launch of its revamped Master of Business Administration program, now available in two modalities. The fully online MBA program now requires 30 credits to complete — reduced from 36 — allowing students to earn their master’s degrees sooner while saving on tuition costs. In addition to the reduction in required credits, students can also finish faster by transferring up to 12 credits, including up to 6 from certifications such as the CPA and SHRM-CP. The first start date for the program is August 31, 2026.

The revised MBA will be offered in two fully online formats, allowing students to learn the way that best fits their learning style, schedule and career goals: An instructor-led credit-based option, and a self-paced competency-based option, known as UMass Global MyPath. Both formats offer a rigorous curriculum mapped to industry standards, featuring project-based learning that turns concepts into real work, giving students knowledge they can put to work right away.

"We kept what makes an MBA worth having and built it for the way people work and hire today,” explained Dr. Amy Burks-Stewart, the acting dean for the School of Business and Professional Studies at UMass Global. “Students earn the full degree in 30 credits, so they finish sooner and spend less.”

Additionally, students earn five digital badges throughout the course of the program. Distributed by Credly, these micro-credentials are employer-validated proof of their workforce skills that can be shared before they even finish the program.

“Students will earn verified micro-credentials along the way in the core areas of business, from financial decision-making to data analytics to leadership and growth,” noted Dr. Burks-Stewart. “For a hiring manager, that means a candidate who can point to exactly what they can do. For a student, it means a respected degree and real proof of skill, earned at the same time."

Prospective students can visit the Master of Business Administration program page for more information or speak with an enrollment coach to get started.

About University of Massachusetts Global

Accredited by WSCUC, University of Massachusetts Global is a private, nonprofit affiliate of the University of Massachusetts system, committed to helping adult learners change their lives through education. The university offers over 55 online programs tailored for workplace relevance — associate, bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral degrees, along with teaching credentials, stackable certificates, and authorizations. All coursework is 100 percent online, which meshes with the busy lives of non‑traditional students. UMass Global is known for attentive student support, accommodating transfer policies, high graduation rates, alumni satisfaction, and low student loan default rates.

The full Standards and Policy of Academic Integrity text was instead located, current and public, in the 2026-2027 Academic Catalog (catalog.umassglobal.edu), read in-browser since the catalog's landing page returns an interstitial to a plain fetch; this is the version quoted throughout section 02.
Source: Center for Instructional Innovation — Academic Integrity (Faculty). The linked Turnitin materials are the vendor's own content, curated here as a faculty resource; they are not quoted as UMass Global's own statement, and no UMass Global-authored sentence on the evidentiary weight of an AI-detection result was located on this page or in the Standards and Policy of Academic Integrity (quoted in full below).

The Standards and Policy of Academic Integrity itself (in the public 2026-2027 Academic Catalog; retrieved Oct 25, 2026) governs AI use directly without naming a detection tool:

"Submitting work completed using any AI tool without instructor permission is prohibited. When faculty require the use of technology, including artificial intelligence, as a part of an assignment for the course, there is no violation. Students are reminded to consult syllabi, assignment sheets/rubrics, program documents and their faculty. Use of artificial intelligence, when permitted, must be correctly cited in the assignment."

UMass Global's Standards and Policy of Academic Integrity (2026-2027 Academic Catalog; retrieved Oct 25, 2026) places the first determination with the instructor: faculty "investigating the incident(s), determining through evidence, subject matter expertise, and professional experience whether or not a violation of this policy has occurred." No evidentiary standard — such as a preponderance of the evidence — is named anywhere in the policy for either the Dean's review or the GAC hearing; this is a genuine absence, stated rather than assumed. The GAC panel instead decides "based on whether or not a violation(s) actually occurred, evidence and appropriate information provided during the Dean's review and/or during the GAC hearing, university policies, and procedures."

"If the student does not agree with the sanctions imposed by the instructor... the student may work with an advisor to submit a petition within 10 business days of being informed of the imposed sanction." "[T]he student may request a hearing with the Governance and Appeals Committee (GAC), within 10 business days of receiving the Dean's decision." "A student has the right to appeal within 30 business days of notification by the GAC of the academic integrity decision... The appeal decision will be rendered by the Office of the Executive Vice Chancellor of Academic Affairs. The appeal decision will be final and binding."

Source: Undergraduate Credit-Hour and MyPath Academic Policies and Procedures. What these quotations mean for any particular case is for the institution and its process to determine; they are reproduced so you can read the originals in context.

University of Massachusetts Global charges $500 a credit for undergraduate courses in its 2026-27 catalog, and 56% of all students who started in 2017-18 earned an award within eight years (College Scorecard, October 15, 2026 release). Scorecard’s average net price for 2024-25 is $35,957, because it counts living costs on top of tuition.

If you are paying with your own money this time, you will want to know whether this is UMass. UMass Global calls itself “a private, nonprofit affiliate of the University of Massachusetts.”

College Scorecard and College Navigator list it as public, and its accreditor, WSCUC, classifies its financial structure as non-profit with a “Multi-institution System” sponsorship.

## UMass Global is a UMass affiliate that federal data lists as public

The University of Massachusetts and Chapman University announced on September 2, 2021 “the transfer of control of Brandman University to UMass,” which launched UMass Global as “a nonprofit affiliate of UMass.” All of its coursework is online.

## UMass Global’s 2026-27 catalog charges $500 a credit for undergraduate courses

Instructor-led courses run in 8-week sessions. UMass Global says “Most instructor-led online programs offer three to six start dates each year, and once enrolled, students progress through six 8-week sessions annually.”

UMass Global tuition, 2026-27 catalog (rates may change without notice)

Program  | Regular rate  | Reduced rate
--- | --- | ---
Associate and bachelor's, per credit  | $500  | $250, active-duty military and spouses
On top of tuition, it charges a $145 technology fee each session ($215 each MyPath billing period) and a $150 degree conferral fee, and exempts active-duty undergraduate and master’s students from the technology fee.

This example assumes UMass Global accepts every one of your earlier credits toward a 120-credit bachelor’s, leaving 60; the school decides how many count. Instructor-led rows assume two 3-credit courses a session, so 10 sessions.

Example: 60 credits left at 2026-27 catalog rates, before any aid (by our math)

Option  | Sum  | Total

Regular rate  | 60 x $500 + $1,450 technology fees + $150 conferral  | $31,600
Active duty  | 60 x $250 + $150 conferral; technology fee waived  | $15,150
Military spouse  | 60 x $250 + $1,450 technology fees + $150 conferral (the catalog waives the fee for active-duty students only)  | $16,600

The MyPath row leaves out the $150 conferral fee.

Scorecard lists tuition and fees of $12,560 for 2025-26. Our guide to how many credits transfer explains how a credit evaluation works.


UMass Global says your own cost of attendance “can be found in self-service after you have been awarded assistance.” Our guide to cost of attendance for online students explains what each budget line covers.

## Undergraduate MyPath charges $3,500 per 24-week period, and you pay before you start

MyPath is UMass Global’s competency-based, self-paced format; its MyPath page lists one associate, two bachelor’s and two master’s programs. The catalog says “The student pays for the time, not by credit hour or by course.”

These rules come from the catalog’s undergraduate competency-based policies:

  * Pay first. Tuition must be paid in full, or your aid applied to a zero balance, before you can start your competencies.
  * Keep moving. If you do not complete a payment period within 24 instructional weeks, you must meet with the “appropriate School Dean and/or Dean’s Designee.” After 28 consecutive days without contact with your academic coach and the course material, you are withdrawn the next business day.
  * Inactivity and aid. The “Return to [Button: Title IV]Title IV, Title IV of the Higher Education Act. The part of federal law that covers federal student aid. A Title IV school is one approved to pay out federal grants and loans.” process starts after 14 consecutive days without educational activity.
  * Refunds. You can drop all competencies “within 30 days of the start of the student’s first billing period and receive a full tuition refund. This applies only to the first billing period.”
  * One format at a time. MyPath students “cannot be enrolled in a credit-hour program or take credit hour courses due to financial aid requirements and restrictions.”
  * Transfer later. Competency units “may not equate to a credit-bearing course for transfer purposes.”

Our guide to financial aid for competency-based degrees explains how federal aid pays for self-paced programs.

## Who UMass Global fits, and the watch-outs

### It fits if

  * You serve on active duty or are a military spouse. Undergraduate credit-hour courses cost $250 a credit for you in the 2026-27 catalog. In 2023-24, 234 undergraduates used Tuition Assistance; our guide to military Tuition Assistance covers the caps.
  * You are coming back with credits. 694 undergraduates transferred in for fall 2024, and College Navigator lists credit for life experiences among the credit UMass Global accepts.

### Watch-outs

  * Master’s fields carry the most debt in the table. Graduates of the mental and social health master’s who finished in 2022-23 and 2023-24 owed a median $61,500.
  * Refunds end after week two. In credit-hour courses (not MyPath), drop before day one for 100% back, in week one for 90% and in week two for 80%; after that, nothing.
  * The information form names a second company. It asks you to consent to “calls, texts, emails and advertising from UMass Global and/or Kaplan North America, LLC,” and says consent “is not required to attend.”

## Check your own aid before you apply to UMass Global

UMass Global’s averages describe other students. The aid check applies the federal rules for the year you start (2026-27 or 2027-28) to your answers, takes about two minutes, and asks no name, email or phone number for the result.

For 2026-27, Pell pays up to $7,395 a year. UMass Global’s financial aid office sets your actual offer.

StudentAid.gov says Pell Grants “usually are awarded only to undergraduate students who display exceptional financial need and have not earned a bachelor’s, graduate, or professional degree,” though a student in a “postbaccalaureate teacher certification program” might get one.

On the same measures, College Scorecard’s October 2026 data puts the University of Arizona Global Campus at a 21% eight-year rate for students who started in 2017-18 and $29,813 in median federal debt for graduates who entered repayment in fiscal 2024 and 2025.

The same data puts Purdue University Global at 30% and $25,625 on the same cohorts.

Degree Sources may refer readers to schools through partners. School matching is optional, comes after your aid result, and is not an application or admission to UMass Global or any school. The figures here come from federal data, WSCUC and UMass Global’s own catalog and pages, and this profile does not rank schools.

## UMass Global requirements in detail

Translation

UMass Global states no translation rule; the evaluation agency needs the translation before it evaluates a document not in English.

Who may translate

Set by the agency: WES wants a professional translator; IERF asks for word-for-word translations and may require professional ones; TEC asks for an ATA-certified translator.

Evaluation

From IERF, WES or another NACES member, course by course, no older than one year, including a copy of the official documents used (UMass Global catalog 2026-2027: admission).

Partner agency

The Evaluation Company, with discounted new evaluations through UMass Global's link (International admission).

Foreign high school

Documentation from an approved foreign evaluation service showing the equivalent of a US high school diploma (Undergraduate admission).

Graduate

A bachelor's degree from abroad may qualify if the official evaluation shows it is equivalent (Graduate admission).

Visas

UMass Global is not SEVP-approved and does not admit visitor or exchange students (UMass Global catalog 2026-2027: admission).

## Every level goes through the evaluation

UMass Global is fully online.

Its catalog asks every applicant with international academic history, at the bachelor's, master's and doctoral level, for a completed transcript evaluation from IERF, WES or another NACES member, and says the evaluation is what determines eligibility for admission (catalog, admission).

The report must be course by course, no more than one year old, and must include a copy of the official documents the agency used.

For undergraduates without college credit, high school completion can be shown with a document from an approved foreign evaluation service (undergraduate admission).

Graduate applicants need a bachelor's degree; one earned abroad may qualify if the official evaluation shows it is equivalent (graduate admission).

UMass Global defines international students as those living outside the US without US citizenship, permanent residence or protected status, and opens only some programs to them (UMass Global catalog 2026-2027: admission).

## Frequently asked questions

Which evaluation agencies does UMass Global accept?

IERF, WES or any other NACES member; The Evaluation Company is its discount partner (UMass Global catalog 2026-2027: admission, partner).

Can I use an eVerbary translation for WES?

Yes. WES accepts translations from a professional translation service (WES).

Can I reuse an evaluation I ordered years ago?

No. UMass Global accepts evaluations no older than one year (UMass Global catalog 2026-2027: admission).

Can UMass Global give me an F-1 visa?

No. It is not an SEVP-approved school (UMass Global catalog 2026-2027: admission).

Is my bachelor's from abroad enough for a master's at UMass Global?

It may be, if the official evaluation shows it is equivalent to a US bachelor's (Graduate admission).

Will eVerbary convert my grades to a US GPA?

No. The translation reproduces the grades and the grading scale exactly as they appear. A GPA conversion is credential evaluation, which the institution or an evaluation agency does.
